```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md (§3, R1–R11); ranking in your partner's words, 2026-11-06 ("Rank them in the order you listed"). Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). | uv workspace with four package scaffolds (`packages/*`).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A historical baseline of archived quarterly filing indexes over a configured range (R1) | A | 1 | Requests: one quarterly `master.idx` per quarter plus listings; about 136 quarters if the range starts in 1993, so under a minute at 3 req/s (§4.3). Byte volume measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs (R2) | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year; request time negligible at 3 req/s. Volume measured by Stage 1 |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index catalog in Parquet built from the ingested indexes (R3) | A | 3 | Compute and peak memory measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The pipeline running on the Azure services the ADR names (R4) | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated before a real run; measured by Stage 8's smoke test |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher (R5) | A | 5 | Engineering time only |
| O6 | Reprocessing from retained original bytes with no new download (R6) | A | 6 | Raw storage is about the O1 + O2 byte volume plus changed snapshots; measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Periodic reconciliation of the quarterly baseline (R7) | A | 7 | Weekly re-read of every supported quarter: about 136 requests, under a minute at 3 req/s |
| O8 | All SEC traffic through one downloader and one request budget (R8) | A | 8 | Bounded by the SEC ceiling of 10 req/s, with a target of 3 req/s (§4.3) |
| O9 | Readers resolving a versioned quarter manifest through one active pointer (R9) | A | 9 | Engineering time only |
| O10 | Closed-quarter withdrawals that wait for hash-bound approval (R10) | A | 10 | Your partner's time per approval; frequency unknown until O7 runs |
| O11 | The stated defaults as validated configuration (R11) | A | 11 | Engineering time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression). One track: every outcome serves the same catalog.

## Open questions

These were not part of the earlier batched question set. Each has a default, so neither blocks Stage 1.

1. **Package home.** §4.9 proposes `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repository also has scaffolds for `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, `sec-edgar-client` and `sec-edgar-download`, and a root script `sec-edgar = "sec_edgar:main"` whose module does not exist. Default: Stage 1's brainstorming settles where the code lives and what happens to the unused scaffolds.
2. **Acceptance.** The ADR and the spec are both Proposed, and §7 step 1 accepts them before building. Default: Stages 1–7 run locally and proceed. Stage 8 consumes acceptance.

## Stages

Order diverges from the ranking (O1…O11), for dependency reasons:
- O4 (Azure, rank 4) moves to Stage 8, because the local stages give cheap real-data information and do not wait on the Proposed ADR.
- O9 publication (Stage 5) precedes O7 and O10, because reconciliation compares candidates against the active catalog.
- O11 configuration moves up to Stage 3, because the range and handoff keys gate Stage 4.
- O8's shared lease waits for Stage 7, because only then do concurrent collectors exist.

Ranks 1–3 still lead, as the core stage.

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter and one real daily index to canonical Parquet
      Objective: Download one archived quarterly and one daily master index from the SEC and produce canonical rows locally, at the smallest usable standard.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing (repository scaffolds only)
      Produces: retained raw snapshots with SHA-256; a parser emitting the §4.5 canonical row contract; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — one archived quarter's index is fetched with an identifying User-Agent at ≤3 req/s, and its original bytes and hash are stored. O3 — the quarterly and daily files both yield Parquet with the §4.5 canonical columns. The findings file records byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory and request count for the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay identities → Stage 2; configuration validation, retries and §5 error outcomes → Stage 3; range backfill, daily catch-up and historical golden fixtures → Stage 4; generations and active pointer → Stage 5; reconciliation and withdrawals → Stage 6; shared lease → Stage 7; Azure services → Stage 8; monitoring, runbooks and scheduling → Stages 8–9
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Source manifest and replay
      Objective: Record source, snapshot and processing identity (§4.5) so that stored inputs reprocess without SEC access (§4.6 Transform).
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1 raw snapshots and parser
      Produces: manifest records with `downloaded -> transformed` states; observation output keyed by snapshot, parser and schema
      Exit: O6 — a parser-version change reprocesses Stage 1's snapshots with zero SEC requests, and repeated runs give an identical logical catalog (§6 Replay).
      Leaves out: `published` state → Stage 5; Table Storage backing and execution/image identifiers → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: Validated configuration and resilient collection
      Objective: Validate the §4.8 settings before any network I/O, and map collection failures to the §5 named outcomes.
      Outcomes: O11
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader; Stage 2 manifest (attempt and failure state)
      Produces: typed configuration; a bounded retry policy; §5 Configuration, Not yet available, Throttled, Access blocked and Invalid source outcomes
      Exit: O11 — every §5 Configuration case is refused before any request, and the retry, Retry-After, attempt-bound and 403-halt cases pass against mocked responses.
      Leaves out: shared budget across collectors → Stage 7; schedule keys taking effect → Stages 8–9
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Range backfill and daily catch-up
      Objective: Ingest a configured quarter range and discover daily indexes with catch-up, through one shared code path (§4.2, §4.4 Identity and Open quarter, §4.6 Parse).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O5
      Consumes: Stages 1–3; the backfill range and handoff date recorded per §7 step 1
      Produces: `discover` and `collect` worksets; resolved observations for the open and closed quarters
      Exit: O1 — a backfill over the configured range reports complete, pending and failed units, and golden fixtures cover the range's formats. O2 — daily discovery catches up across a quarter boundary and a multi-quarter outage, and a failed listing does not advance the boundary (§6 Discovery). O5 — the backfill and daily workflows invoke the same collect and transform commands.
      Leaves out: generation publication → Stage 5; reconciliation → Stage 6
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Quarter generations and active pointer
      Objective: Publish complete quarter generations behind one conditionally updated pointer (§4.5 paths, §4.6 Publish).
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 4 observations; Stage 2 manifest
      Produces: generation paths, manifest.json and changes.parquet; a pointer store with conditional write; the `published` state
      Exit: O9 — crashes injected at the three §6 Publication points leave only complete generations readable, and competing publishers lose no update.
      Leaves out: withdrawal gate → Stage 6; Table Storage as the pointer backend → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Refresh quarterly sources against the active catalog under the §4.4 Closed-quarter and Changes rules (§4.2 Reconciliation).
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 4–5
      Produces: a reconciliation workflow; `awaiting_approval` candidates; approval records
      Exit: O7 — an unchanged hash skips transformation, and a changed snapshot records its additions and updates in the change report. O10 — removals in a closed quarter stay gated until approval names the exact hash; open-quarter absence never withdraws; stale daily replay cannot resurrect a key (§6 Reconciliation).
      Leaves out: weekly trigger → Stage 9
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: One request budget across collectors
      Objective: Make concurrent backfill, daily and reconciliation collectors share one lease-governed SEC budget (§4.3 One request budget).
      Outcomes: O8
      Consumes: Stages 3, 4 and 6 collectors
      Produces: a renewable lease and coordination namespace; daily-first turn ordering
      Exit: O8 — under concurrent collectors, no two request issuers overlap, retries count toward the budget, and a lost lease stops requests (§6 Access).
      Leaves out: Storage-account backing in Azure → Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Azure deployment and live smoke test
      Objective: Run the shared image under ADF and Container Apps Jobs with ADLS, Table Storage and Monitor, in an isolated environment (§4.1, §4.7, §4.9, §7 steps 2–5).
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–7; the ADR and spec accepted, with the deployment values recorded (§7 step 1)
      Produces: versioned infrastructure with triggers disabled; alerts; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-8-findings.md
      Exit: O4 — ADF starts and polls a job to a terminal outcome that is checked against its worker result file; the §6 integration tests pass; the live smoke test (one quarter, one daily index) and its raw replay record byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, image digest, request rate and Azure cost in the findings file.
      Leaves out: production backfill, enabled triggers and runbooks → Stage 9
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 9: Baseline campaign and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the production backfill and daily catch-up, then enable the schedules and document operations (§7 steps 6–9, §8).
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7
      Consumes: Stage 8 deployment and its smoke-test findings
      Produces: the release record (image, configuration and active generations); runbooks per §8
      Exit: O1 — every requested baseline unit is published, or the incomplete range is recorded as approved. O2 — the daily trigger is enabled after catch-up acceptance, and observed scheduled runs match their reports. O7 — one manual reconciliation has run, its gated candidates are resolved, and the weekly trigger is enabled.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note (or, for a writing-plans stage, the plan header) carries:

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

With every stage ticked, run SKILL.md §6 over the Outcomes list (O1–O11): give each outcome a verdict with evidence (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items), and also check the spec's §7 Exit bullets. Each unmet outcome either becomes a new stage or is deferred with a written reason. Then retire this roadmap with the spec and ADR to `specs/completed/`.
```
